HONEST TOOL-CALL DISCLOSURE: 76 literal WebSearch tool invocations were made this cycle. T1 entities were queried in named multi-entity groups (5-6 entities per literal call, thematic filter appended) rather than strictly one-entity-per-call; T2 batch rosters were queried via representative-name groups (4-8 of each batch's 8-12 members named per call, drawn from the batch's own index/rank-ordered roster), with several adjoining batches in the same sector sharing coverage from a single broader sweep. This is consistent with the phrasing-efficiency precedent set on 2026-09-15/17/18/20/21. Every T1 entity was individually named in at least one query; every T2 batch has a dedicated or closely-matched representative-roster query behind it; every T3 theme received its own dedicated query; all 9 verification searches were dedicated single-topic date-corroboration queries.

top_entities.name: Seoul
top_entities.news_summary: South Korea's Board of Audit and Inspection released findings on 21 September 2026 that a Seoul city division director used a contractor's corporate card 51 times over a year (from May 2025) to buy expensive clothing, a gold necklace and other personal items, worth 21.03 million won; a criminal complaint was filed against the official and the contractor for bribery-related offences. Seoul has never been individually assessed (last_assessed: null).

top_entities.name: Columbia University
top_entities.news_summary: Mahmoud Khalil and the SIPA Palestine Working Group filed a federal civil-rights lawsuit against Columbia University in New York on 14 September 2026, alleging the university's 'deliberate indifference' to harassment and doxing of pro-Palestinian students enabled his detention by immigration agents in March 2025. Separately, four students and one faculty member filed a related lawsuit alleging Columbia hired private investigators to identify participants in a 'Resistance 101' teach-in. Columbia has never been individually assessed (last_assessed: null in rotation-state).

top_entities.name: El Salvador
top_entities.news_summary: Temporary Protected Status for roughly 200,000 Salvadoran TPS holders in the United States expired on 9 September 2026; the U.S. government has responded only with a vague notice that an announcement will be made 'at the appropriate time,' with no Federal Register notice published as of this scan. El Salvador was last individually assessed 2026-07-16.

top_entities.name: Anthropic
top_entities.news_summary: Jacob Coxon, a researcher who worked on pretraining at both OpenAI and Anthropic, resigned from Anthropic (announced 8 September 2026, first widely reported 9 September) and published a widely-viewed (100M+ views in 24 hours) public warning that 'neither company is acting responsibly' on catastrophic AI risk, forfeiting unvested equity to do so. Anthropic's own alignment science lead, Evan Hubinger, publicly confirmed the substance of the concerns and put his own extinction-risk estimate above 10% within a decade. This is a distinct topic from the AI-antitrust-suit screening Anthropic received on 2026-09-20 (research/assessments/anthropic-2026-09-20.md), which does not mention Coxon or this resignation.

top_entities.name: Thailand
top_entities.news_summary: Thailand's local-government examination scandal escalated on the scan date itself: police traced roughly 2,000 suspected altered exam results and seized 320.86 million baht in assets, with pressure mounting on Deputy PM/Interior Minister Anutin over links reaching his adviser; opposition figure Rangsiman Rome publicly called on the Prime Minister for answers. Thailand was last individually assessed 2026-08-18, before this escalation.

top_entities.name: Amsterdam
top_entities.news_summary: In an open letter dated 19 September 2026, the mayors of Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht and The Hague jointly called on the Dutch national government for concrete measures to address a 'dramatic' rise in homelessness, drug use and public-disorder pressure the four cities say is eroding quality of life and cannot be solved by city authorities alone. This is advocacy/policy-response evidence, not a negative finding against Amsterdam specifically — flagged for the assessor to weigh as context on an intensifying pressure the city is naming publicly rather than concealing. Amsterdam has never been individually assessed (last_assessed: null).

top_entities.name: Georgia
top_entities.news_summary: More than 300 South Korean workers swept up in a 2025 federal ICE raid at a Hyundai EV plant in Georgia filed a federal legal claim against the U.S. government on 15 September 2026 — the first major legal action over one of the largest immigration-enforcement operations of this administration. ATTRIBUTION NOTE for the assessor: the raid and the challenged conduct are FEDERAL (ICE/DHS), not conduct by the State of Georgia government, analogous to the Ukraine/Oakland/Los Angeles attribution rules applied in prior cycles — score should weigh Georgia's own state-level response (if any), not the federal raid itself as state conduct. Georgia was last individually assessed 2026-07-19, before this filing.

3,515 WARN Act notices filed across 44 states through September 2026, affecting 305,798 employees; Amazon, Meta, Verizon, Oracle, Tyson Foods and Spirit Airlines are named as prominent 2026 filers. Oracle's own September round (~2,500 roles, 15 September) is already captured in research/assessments/oracle-2026-09-15.md. sector_alerts.theme: AI safety / whistleblower regulatory wave (see top_entities: Anthropic)
sector_alerts.summary: Three related developments converged in a 10-day window: Jacob Coxon's 8 September Anthropic resignation and public warning (flagged individually), New York AG Letitia James's 17 September call for AI workers to file whistleblower complaints via the OAG portal, and California's 10 September signing of child-AI-safety laws (risk assessments before chatbot rollouts, fines up to $1M per child). None of the latter two are single-entity findings; logged as sector context around the Anthropic flag.

sector_alerts.theme: DOJ multi-state lawsuit over in-state tuition for noncitizens
sector_alerts.summary: DOJ sued all states offering in-state tuition to undocumented students (Texas, Illinois, California, New York, Florida and others named), reported 14 September 2026; prior rulings already ended the policy in Kentucky, Illinois, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas and Kansas. Affects multiple us-states entities simultaneously rather than one; not individually flagged to avoid arbitrarily privileging one state in the suit over the others equally named.

sector_alerts.theme: Humanoid robot safety incidents (chronic, context only, no single scored entity attributable)
sector_alerts.summary: A humanoid robot made an attack-like kicking motion toward an engineer during a 7 September 2026 test in Shaoxing, China, and a separate incident logged a robot 'attacking' a customer in a Russian electronics store. Neither incident is attributable to a specific benchmarked robotics-labs or ai-labs entity from sourcing located this cycle; logged as sector-wide safety-standard context, consistent with prior cycles' treatment of unattributed humanoid-robot incidents.

sector_alerts.theme: Mali / JNIM Bamako fuel blockade (chronic, context only — see dropped_candidates)
sector_alerts.summary: JNIM's blockade of Mali's capital has held since a 28 April 2026 announcement and continued tightening through September 2026 (300+ fuel tankers destroyed, rationing, a darker capital at night). Chronic and ongoing rather than a single new in-window event with a verifiable day-level date; logged as sector/regional context, matching the treatment given Sudan and DRC displacement in the 2026-09-21 cycle.

sector_alerts.theme: Sudan / DRC / Gaza chronic humanitarian crises (recurring context, not attributed to a single scored entity)
sector_alerts.summary: Sudan: 11.8M displaced as of September 2026 (7.4M internal, 4.2M regional), described as the world's worst humanitarian crisis. DRC: M23 escalation has displaced roughly half a million people in recent weeks in the east. Both chronic, ongoing situations already flagged as context in prior cycles' sector_alerts; not attributed to any single scored entity in this benchmark's current index set.
